record.paper_title:
AIM Workshop “Pólya-Schur-Lax Problems: Hyperbolicity and Stability
Preservers” — A List of Open Problems
record.context_brief: Hilbert-17th-type factorization through sums of squares
record.original_question:
Let P_n be the set of real polynomials in n variables, P_n^+ the
subset of polynomials nonnegative on all real inputs,
S_n the subset of P_n^+ consisting of sums of squares of polynomials,
and M_n the set of finite-order
constant-coefficient linear partial differential operators T on
R^n[z1, ..., zn] such that T(S_n) ⊆ P_n^+. Is every
nonnegative polynomial P in P_n^+ representable as P = T(S) for some S
in S_n and some T in M_n, equivalently, is M_n ·
S_n = P_n^+ for all n?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each positive integer $n$, let $P_n = \mathbb{R}[z_1,\dots,z_n]$ denote the ring of real polynomials in $n$ variables, and let
\[
P_n^{+} = \{\,P \in P_n : P(x) \ge 0 \text{ for all } x \in \mathbb{R}^n\,\}
\]
be the cone of nonnegative polynomials. Let
\[
S_n = \Big\{\,\textstyle\sum_{i=1}^k Q_i^2 : k \ge 1,\ Q_1,\dots,Q_k \in P_n\,\Big\} \subseteq P_n^{+}
\]
be the set of sums of squares of polynomials. Let $M_n$ be the set of finite-order linear partial differential operators on $P_n$ with constant real coefficients, i.e. operators of the form
\[
T = \sum_{\alpha \in \mathbb{N}^n,\ |\alpha| \le N} c_\alpha\, \partial^{\alpha},\qquad c_\alpha \in \mathbb{R},
\]
for some $N$, which additionally satisfy $T(S_n) \subseteq P_n^{+}$ (that is, $T$ sends every sum of squares to a nonnegative polynomial).

Question: Is it true that for every $n \ge 1$ and every $P \in P_n^{+}$ there exist $T \in M_n$ and $S \in S_n$ with $P = T(S)$? Equivalently, does
\[
M_n \cdot S_n \;=\; P_n^{+}
\]
hold for all $n \ge 1$?

No clear positive or negative resolution was found in the literature accessible via search.
